The meaning quiz displays a kanji and offers other cards' English titles as answers. For new cards, curate **three** semantically
distinct wrong options for the default four-choice quiz. Two remain structurally valid for older cards, but the app fills missing
choices from other cards, preferring shared tags. Exact-title deduplication alone does not establish semantic uniqueness:
different English synonyms can still produce two defensible answers. Keep useful semantic comparisons in the body even when
they are unsuitable as wrong answers.

Kanji-exclusion-aware clients ([Android #132](https://github.com/stop-cran/kanji-cards-android/issues/132)) additionally honor
`quiz_exclusions`, using exact kanji IDs, not word IDs, readings or titles. A declaration on either card excludes that direct pair
both against the target and among chosen distractors, for curated choices and tag/random fallbacks in All, level and custom pools.
Exclusions are symmetric but not transitive: A/B and B/C do not exclude A/C. References must resolve in the complete accepted
source, not the currently filtered pool. A small pool may yield fewer choices, even only the target; the app never restores an
excluded card to fill slots. Exclusions affect meaning choices only, not readings, drawing, membership, ordering or saved progress.

Author a pair only from evidence about the actual displayed labels and ordinary meanings. The observed 剰/冗 fallback ambiguity
motivated this mechanism; it is not automatic synonym discovery or a guarantee for uncurated pairs. Existing older APKs do not
enforce this field. Content depending on it requires the upgraded compatible client; bounded owner-testing acceptance does not
prove compatibility of an older installed app or physical-phone/general-release acceptance.

Editorial review must check the displayed titles against the target's ordinary meanings, not merely look for duplicate strings.
This behavior was checked in [QuizBuilder](https://github.com/stop-cran/kanji-cards-android/blob/8c130a25bdb4e444a80a2f78ef0d11b04bddc12f/app/src/main/java/io/github/stopcran/kanji/core/quiz/QuizBuilder.kt);
larger quizzes or a changed app can still require fallback choices. The validator checks structure, not semantic ambiguity.

### Curated reading questions

Keep complete sourced `onyomi` / `kunyomi` metadata and its order, including rare readings. Use the optional quiz lists to select

comparisons.reason: Requested possible encroachment or violation. The complete card teaches enduring and surpassing, including getting through difficulty (repo/kanji/凌.md:21-30), whereas the independent 侵 character entry specifies unauthorized entry into another's domain (evidence/external-snapshots/01-extract.txt:4-7).
comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: the displayed senses do not themselves establish a collision, but no independent 凌 entry was supplied to settle the suspected ordinary secondary infringement sense. Neither endpoint declares 侵–凌; neither curated set exposes it (repo/kanji/凌.md:1-14; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested invasion or raiding. The card expressly includes taking or plundering and retains おか.す (repo/kanji/略.md:19-35); independent JMdict recognizes 侵略 as invasion, raid and aggression (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:827-866).
comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: the full word corroborates the concern, but does not independently allocate its invasion sense to 略. Its title alone is not exculpatory. Neither endpoint declares 侵–略 and neither curated set exposes it (repo/kanji/略.md:1-12; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested attack or raid. 侵す independently includes raid (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:105-112); 討 actually offers attack, and the supplied shared 討つ/撃つ family independently confirms attack, defeat and conquest rather than discussion alone (repo/kanji/討.md:3; evidence/jmdict-families.xml:590-651).
comparisons.disposition: Collision-needing-exclusion: F1. Attack is a defensible broad answer for raiding, irrespective of the discussion branch. Neither endpoint declares 侵–討; 討's guards involving 攻 and 撃 are not transitive. Neither curated set currently exposes this direct pair (repo/kanji/討.md:1-15; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested harm or damage. Independent JMdict gives 侵す the unrestricted glosses harm, afflict and affect (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:120-126); 損's displayed choice includes damage, and its body and reading rows also include harm and hurt (repo/kanji/損.md:3-35).
comparisons.disposition: Collision-needing-exclusion: F1. The displayed damage branch itself is a defensible rendering of harming; this does not depend on accepting the comparison card as independent dictionary proof. Neither endpoint declares 侵–損; the 侵–害 guard does not protect it. Neither curated set currently exposes the pair (repo/kanji/損.md:1-12; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested harm or hurt. Independent 侵す harm/afflict supports the broad English hurt option (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:120-126; repo/kanji/痛.md:3). The comparison card teaches aching as well as pain and retains いた.める in metadata (repo/kanji/痛.md:10-22).
comparisons.disposition: Collision-needing-exclusion: F1. The displayed word hurt is not limited to the card's aching examples; no claim that all 痛 and 侵 uses coincide is needed. Neither endpoint declares 侵–痛 and neither curated set currently exposes it (repo/kanji/痛.md:1-12; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested affliction or suffering harm. The article includes illness, suffering, a medical patient and both transitive/intransitive 患う uses (repo/kanji/患.md:19-39); independent 侵す includes afflict and affect (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:120-126).
comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: being affected and causing affliction are distinguishable, but that distinction alone cannot rule out every ordinary 患 sense. No independent 患 family was opened. Neither endpoint declares 侵–患; neither curated set exposes it (repo/kanji/患.md:1-12; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested affliction with illness. The card includes disease, falling ill, being troubled, worrying and recovery/addiction expressions, not only the title illness (repo/kanji/病.md:19-38); independent 侵す includes afflict (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:120-126).
comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: illness as the condition is not automatically the action of afflicting, but the supplied evidence does not independently settle 病's full ordinary character senses. Neither endpoint declares 侵–病; neither curated set exposes it (repo/kanji/病.md:1-12; snapshot/kanji/侵.md:13-14).

comparisons.reason: Requested harm or affliction. The card covers harmfulness, poison, disinfection and the nonliteral 気の毒 expressions, and explicitly distinguishes poison from harm (repo/kanji/毒.md:19-41). comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: substance, harmful property and action must not be conflated, but no independent 毒 entry establishes whether poisoning/harming supplies an ordinary secondary overlap. comparisons.disposition: UNVERIFIED possible collision-needing-exclusion: invasion and occupation are not identical, but the independent whole-word evidence makes dismissal as mere shared subject matter premature; constituent allocation is unresolved. comparisons.reason: Requested intrusion or penetration. The full card includes piercing through, reaching a limit, completion, exclusivity, all-night activity, clarity and figurative strike home (repo/kanji/徹.md:21-34; repo/kanji/徹.md:66-94). comparisons.disposition: Already handled: the ordinary violation branch supports a direct semantic guard even though commit an offense and invade are not unrestricted synonyms. Declared on 侵 at snapshot/kanji/侵.md:14, not on 犯 (repo/kanji/犯.md:1-12). Neither curated set exposes the pair.

comparisons.reason: Requested shared harm/affliction. comparisons.disposition: Already handled: a necessary direct guard for the shared harm answer; killing and obstructing are not thereby assigned to 侵. Declared on 侵 at snapshot/kanji/侵.md:14, not on 害 (repo/kanji/害.md:1-12). Neither curated set exposes the pair.

Independent 攻める confirms attack and assault; independent 侵す includes raid (evidence/jmdict-families.xml:42-77; evidence/jmdict-families.xml:105-112).
comparisons.disposition: Already handled: raiding supports a broad attack choice; neither special study nor colloquial boldness is assigned to 侵. Conservative invasion/attack guard declared on 侵 at snapshot/kanji/侵.md:14, not on 攻 (repo/kanji/攻.md:1-15). Neither curated set exposes the pair.

comparisons.reason: Requested attack/raid. The article includes shooting, striking, counterattack, sensory impact and defeat (repo/kanji/撃.md:21-23; repo/kanji/撃.md:40-45). Independent KANJIDIC2 includes attack and conquest, and the supplied 討つ/撃つ family includes attack (evidence/kanjidic2-records.xml:893-977; evidence/jmdict-families.xml:590-651).
comparisons.disposition: Already handled: attack/raid supports the conservative guard; invasion need not involve shooting and no universal equivalence is asserted. Declared on 侵 at snapshot/kanji/侵.md:14, not on 撃 (repo/kanji/撃.md:1-15). Neither curated set exposes the pair.

comparisons.reason: Requested entry/intrusion. The article includes entering, putting in, literary いる and the recorded ジュ example (repo/kanji/入.md:19-34). Independent 侵's definition explicitly involves entering another's domain without permission, and independent 入 has enter/insert (evidence/external-snapshots/01-extract.txt:4-7; evidence/kanjidic2-records.xml:290-373).
comparisons.disposition: Already handled: enter is a defensible broad component of the intrusion action although entry need not be unauthorized; this is a conservative guard, not a claim that put in universally means invade. Declared on 侵 at snapshot/kanji/侵.md:14, not on 入 (repo/kanji/入.md:1-12). Neither curated set exposes the pair.
